text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- President Jacques Chirac, in a television address last night, warned against a possible return to power of the Socialists, called for cuts in taxes to bring them in line with other European countries. He added he was seeking an economy based on initiative and freedom but allowing for social solidarity. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation, The IHT.)
LES ECHOS
-- President Jacques Chirac warns against a possible return to power of Socialist, calls for cuts in taxes to bring them in line with other European countries.
-- Consumer spending rose 1.5 percent in April, higher than forecast.

-- Socialist party leader Lional Jospin seen favourite to be named prime minister if Socialists win parliamentary election while National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin tipped to succeed outgoing Prime Minister Alain Juppe if right wins.
LA TRIBUNE

-- Computer services firm Atos (formerly Axime and Sligos) chairman Bernard Bourigeaud says in an interview he plans to sell some non-strategic assets before September as part of restructuring, aims for eight percent operating profit for 1997.
-- Matra Defense Espace chairman Noel Forgeard says agreements in space and missiles between Lagardere and Dasa are unquestionable, whatever outcome of the planned Thomson-CSF privatisation.
-- Number of new life-assurance contracts fell by some 10 percent in the first quarter.
-- Shares in Credit Lyonnais rose by 7.7 percent yesterday and 72.2 percent since start of year amid bullish hopes for 1997 profits.
-- France Telecom questions regulatory authority on the Internet over access terms of other operators to the network through France Telecom's lines.
L'AGEFI
-- CDR company selling off Credit Lyonnais assets sold some 3.5 million Total shares, making an estimated capital gain of one billion francs.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Canal Plus begins selling stake in media group Havas
-- Dassault Aviation chairman Marcel Dassault calls for increased freedom for businesses and better organisation of social benefits, possibly including contributions based on businesses' turnover.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Chirac urges voters not to squander benefits that France is on the point of harvesting, referring to strict budgetary policies and economic modernization.
